data.narrative:
Theion, a Series A climate and energy technology company founded by Ulrich Ehmes, has raised €25M+ to date. The valuation exercise draws on a broader peer universe of nine private-sector climate and energy firms (Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen among them) and one public comparable (LNZA), though narrow-filter peer matching at identical stage and valuation tier yielded insufficient data points for a reliable median-multiple approach.

The applicable method is stage-progression calibration. Using the €25M total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-subsequent-stage advancement, the analysis implies a valuation of €50M. This serves as the central estimate.

The triangulated range spans €42.5M (low) to €57.5M (high), with a median of €50M. This narrow band reflects reliance on a single methodological anchor and limited peer-set granularity within the target sector and stage. Key uncertainties include the absence of same-stage comparables with sufficient data density, which constrains confidence in relative-valuation cross-checks, and the degree to which near-term funding environment and progress on core technical milestones may shift the stage-progression multiplier from 2.0x.
